claim_match_verification.reasoning: The dataset-audit Commons seed (Haeckel Stephoidea) illustrates radiolarian skeletons but is NOT the primary evidence for this slot: Thompson's own Figs. 176-193 (now vendored from ongrowthform1917thom) directly show the echinoderm larval rod framework and the tissue/partition sequences named in the claim. Radiolaria appear in the claim prose and in Ch. V/VI discussion (pp. 264-265 defer skeleton detail to Ch. IX); Commons Challenger Plate 035 and Haeckel Stephoidea are therefore labelled ANALOGUES for the 'radiolarian-like hollow skeleton' clause, not substitutes for the pinned figure range. Measurable variables — radial partition symmetry (Fig. 176 vs 177), triple-junction angles near 120° (Figs. 178-190), isoperimetric circularity of isolated grains (Fig. 180), and hollow-sphere surface-to-volume scaling — are all present on the Thompson plates.
